citations.quote: Backtesting is the practice of evaluating risk measurement procedures by comparing out-of-sample estimates of risk measures with actual realized losses and gains.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Backtesting in the McNeil Ch.9 §9.3 sense compares out-of-sample VaR estimates against realized losses via exceedance counting: under correct calibration the violation indicators form an iid Bernoulli(1−α) process whose count is binomial(T, 1−α).
